preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and n >= 1 and n <= 10**5
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of stones.
Each of the next n lines contains exactly three integers a_i, b_i, c_i (1 ≤ a_i, b_i, c_i ≤ 10^9) representing the edge lengths of the i-th stone.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(a) <= 10**9 and 1 <= int(b) <= 10**9 and 1 <= int(c) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for a, b, c in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each edge length a_i, b_i, c_i is a positive integer between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is either '1' (selecting one stone) or '2' (selecting two stones).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1].split())
postconditions.description: The second line of output contains k distinct integers from 1 to n (where k is 1 or 2), representing the indices of the selected stones.

postconditions.expression: k == 1 and max_sphere_radius_single == max(max_sphere_radius_single, max_sphere_radius_double) or k == 2 and max_sphere_radius_double == max(max_sphere_radius_single, max_sphere_radius_double)
postconditions.description: The selected stones maximize the radius of the sphere that can be carved from the resulting parallelepiped. If k=1, the radius is the minimum of the three edge lengths of the selected stone. If k=2, the radius is the minimum of the three edge lengths of the combined parallelepiped (after gluing two stones on a matching face).

postconditions.expression: max_sphere_radius_single == max(min(int(a), int(b), int(c)) for a, b, c in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
postconditions.description: max_sphere_radius_single is the maximum possible radius of a sphere carved from a single stone, computed as the minimum of the three edge lengths of that stone.

postconditions.expression: max_sphere_radius_double == max(min(x, y, z) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n) for x, y, z in [get_combined_dimensions(i, j)])
postconditions.description: max_sphere_radius_double is the maximum possible radius of a sphere carved from two glued stones, computed as the minimum of the three edge lengths of the combined parallelepiped after gluing stones i and j on a matching face. get_combined_dimensions(i, j) returns the three edge lengths of the combined parallelepiped after optimally gluing stones i and j.

postconditions.expression: k == 1 and selected_stone_indices == [i+1] and min(int(a), int(b), int(c)) == max_sphere_radius_single for i, (a, b, c) in enumerate([line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) if min(int(a), int(b), int(c)) == max_sphere_radius_single
postconditions.description: If k=1, the selected stone is one that maximizes the minimum of its three edge lengths.

postconditions.expression: k == 2 and selected_stone_indices == [i+1, j+1] and min(x, y, z) == max_sphere_radius_double for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n) for x, y, z in [get_combined_dimensions(i, j)] if min(x, y, z) == max_sphere_radius_double
postconditions.description: If k=2, the selected stones are a pair that, when optimally glued, maximizes the minimum of the three edge lengths of the combined parallelepiped.
